mutations.name: the epoch guard is dropped — a mint that was in flight across an account switch repopulates the cache, so the PREVIOUS account's credential rides the next tenant's request. Silent, cross-account, and invisible without this guard
mutations.anchor: if (epoch !== _userJwtEpoch) return null; // account changed under us

mutations.name: in-flight coalescing is dropped — a concurrent burst on a cold cache mints once per caller instead of once, multiplying auth RPCs against the upstream at exactly the moment a pool is recovering
a JWT with no readable exp gets cached anyway — a credential we cannot age out is presented until the process restarts, so a rotated or revoked token keeps being sent
the #21 field is emitted even for an empty JWT — a zero-length field 21 appears on the DEFAULT path, changing a working wire for every operator who never enabled the switch

the switch accepts any truthy-ish value instead of exactly '1' — the same Number()/falsy rewrite that silently flipped sibling knobs in #241/#242, here turning a wire-changing credential on for an operator who set it to '0' or 'false'
